falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Increase per-subject calibration sample size 5x using pooled data across all subjects (no covariate stratification) and evaluate empirical coverage on test subjects across the full range of covariate distances. If coverage is restored to nominal level (e.g., 90%) uniformly across all covariate distances, the proposed mechanism (exchangeability violation due to inter-subject heterogeneity) is falsified; the rival (insufficient per-subject sample size) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Empirical coverage remains at nominal level (≥90%) for all test subjects regardless of Wasserstein distance between calibration and test subject feature distributions when per-subject calibration size is increased 5x with pooled data.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Multi-subject physiological dataset with ≥50 subjects spanning diverse age, BMI, medication, pathology; subject-level covariates; continuous physiological signals (ECG, PPG, ABP) with ≥5-minute segments per subject; ground truth labels synchronized with signals; calibration and test splits with controlled covariate shift (e.g., leave-one-subject-out, stratified by covariate bins).
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Site or device differences (e.g., electrode type, device model) confound with subject covariates, creating apparent heterogeneity that is actually a technical artifact; controlling for site_id and device_model mitigates but may not eliminate if unmeasured.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient statistical power to detect coverage degradation if the effect size of covariate shift is small relative to sampling variability, or if the Wasserstein distance metric does not capture the relevant physiological heterogeneity dimensions.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Stratify test segments by both signal quality index (SQI) bins and physiological state (e.g., heart rate bins). Fit a standard conformal predictor on all calibration data. If conditional coverage equalizes within heart rate bins but remains heterogeneous across SQI bins, the proposed mechanism (sensor noise heteroscedasticity) is falsified; the rival (physiological state change) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Conditional coverage does not differ significantly across SQI bins (p > 0.05, chi-square test) after stratifying on heart rate bins, or coverage equalizes within heart rate bins but not SQI bins.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Wearable multi-sensor dataset (ECG, PPG, 3-axis accelerometer) with synchronized reference labels; signal quality indices per segment; accelerometer magnitude per segment; activity labels or continuous activity intensity; calibration and test segments spanning full activity range with ≥20% high-artifact segments.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Sensor type, placement, or skin condition affect both artifact magnitude and SQI, creating a spurious association between SQI and coverage; controlling for sensor_type and placement_site reduces but may not eliminate this confounding.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: SQI does not accurately capture the true artifact severity (e.g., motion artifacts with normal SQI), or the physiological state bins are too coarse to reveal the true conditional coverage pattern.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Augment the daytime-only calibration set with nighttime segments matched in sample size per circadian phase bin (e.g., equal number of segments per 4-hour block). Re-evaluate conditional coverage across all phase bins using standard marginal conformal prediction. If coverage equalizes across all circadian phases without phase-aware nonconformity scores, the proposed mechanism (inherent circadian non-stationarity) is falsified; the rival (sample selection bias) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage is homogeneous across all circadian phase bins (p > 0.05, chi-square test) when calibration data includes matched day and night segments, and the maximum coverage difference across bins is ≤5 percentage points.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Longitudinal physiological dataset ≥48 hours per subject with continuous signals and reference labels; time-of-day timestamps; sleep stage annotations; circadian phase estimates (e.g., dim light melatonin onset, core body temperature minimum, or actigraphy-derived phase); calibration data restricted to daytime (8am-8pm) and test data spanning 24h.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Shift work, sleep disorders, or medication timing alter circadian phase independently of time-of-day, making phase estimates noisy and masking true non-stationarity; controlling for schedule and diagnosed disorders helps but residual confounding likely.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Circadian phase estimation error (e.g., using only time-of-day without physiological markers) dilutes the phase-coverage relationship, or the ultradian component (90-min cycles) drives coverage variation that is not captured by 4-hour circadian bins.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: On a dataset with replicate reference measurements, simulate label noise with known heteroscedasticity and state-dependence (correlated with clinical concern flag). Compare three nonconformity scores on a perfectly calibrated predictor: (a) standard absolute residual, (b) variance-normalized score (residual / predicted model standard deviation), (c) label-noise-aware score (residual / sqrt(model variance + estimated label noise variance)). If (b) matches (c) in restoring conditional coverage given concern flag, the proposed mechanism (label noise as distinct cause) is falsified; the rival (model heteroscedasticity) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Variance-normalized nonconformity score (b) achieves conditional coverage within 5 percentage points of the label-noise-aware score (c) for high-concern segments, and both significantly outperform standard score (a).
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Dataset with continuous wearable signals and sparse reference measurements (e.g., cuff BP, arterial line); exact timestamps for references and signals; clinical concern flags; reference device type and calibration records; replicate reference measurements (within 5 min) to estimate label noise variance.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Reference device calibration drift or clinician triggering bias creates label noise that correlates with true state, mimicking state-dependent heteroscedasticity; controlling for device_type and concern_flag isolates but may not fully separate.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Replicate measurements are too sparse to reliably estimate label noise distribution per segment, or the simulation assumptions (e.g., noise distribution shape) do not match reality, leading to incorrect conclusion about score performance.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Balance the calibration set 1:1 across disease labels (e.g., heart failure, sepsis, atrial fibrillation) via oversampling minority subpopulations. Apply standard marginal conformal prediction and evaluate conditional coverage per disease label and severity stratum on the test set. If coverage equalizes across all subpopulations (max-min coverage difference ≤5 points), the proposed mechanism (fundamentally different error distributions requiring group-conditional conformal) is falsified; the rival (underrepresentation) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Conditional coverage per disease label does not differ significantly (p > 0.05, chi-square test) after calibration balancing, and worst-case subpopulation coverage is ≥85% when nominal is 90%.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Multi-center physiological dataset with ≥500 patients including diagnosed pathological subpopulations (HF, sepsis, AFib) with prevalence ≥5% each; disease labels and severity scores (NYHA, SOFA); continuous signals and reference labels; calibration and test splits with known disease labels in test set; residuals from base predictor on calibration set for clustering.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Comorbidity burden and disease severity create gradients within labels, so balancing on coarse labels does not address finer heterogeneity; controlling for severity_score and comorbidity_index refines but may not capture all.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Residual clustering does not align with clinical labels, or the base predictor is so misspecified for pathological physiology that even balanced calibration cannot equalize coverage without model improvement.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: In a cohort with scheduled sensor replacements, compare coverage degradation before/after sensor replacement (same physiology, new sensor) versus before/after medication titration (same sensor, changed physiology). If coverage drops significantly only after sensor replacement and not after medication change, the proposed mechanism (physiological adaptation drift) is falsified; the rival (sensor degradation) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Coverage decline correlates with sensor age (days since sensor placement) but not with medication dose changes >20% or clinical deterioration (SOFA increase >2); drift-triggered recalibration based on residuals does not outperform fixed schedule when sensor age is controlled.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Longitudinal dataset ≥30 days per patient with daily calibration updates possible; medication dose records with timestamps; clinical trajectory scores (daily SOFA, NEWS); vascular stiffness indices (PWV, augmentation index) measured periodically; continuous signals and reference labels throughout; sensor replacement logs.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Sensor degradation and physiological adaptation occur simultaneously and are confounded by time; sensor age and medication changes may be correlated (e.g., sicker patients get more medication changes and longer sensor use).
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Drift detection on residuals lacks power (insufficient daily samples) to distinguish gradual physiological drift from sensor drift, or the recalibration trigger threshold is misspecified, leading to false conclusion that drift-triggered recalibration fails.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Train separate predictors for each active modality combination (e.g., PPG+ECG, ECG-only, PPG-only) and apply standard marginal conformal prediction per predictor. Evaluate conditional coverage per modality combination on test data. If coverage equalizes across all combinations (max-min difference ≤5 points), the proposed mechanism (hidden stratification requiring modality-aware conformal scores) is falsified; the rival (model degradation during dropout) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Conditional coverage is homogeneous across modality combinations (p > 0.05, chi-square) when using modality-specific predictors with marginal conformal, and worst-case combination coverage ≥85% at nominal 90%.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Multimodal wearable dataset (PPG, ECG, accelerometer) with synchronized reference labels; modality availability indicators per segment; perfusion index or clinical severity score; interference flags (electrosurgery, MRI); calibration and test sets with ≥5% dropout segments per modality combination.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Skin tone, sensor fit, or environmental interference affect baseline modality quality and dropout probability, creating spurious modality-coverage associations; controlling for signal_quality_per_modality and interference_flag mitigates but residual confounding possible.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient dropout segments per modality combination (especially rare combinations like PPG-only) to estimate coverage reliably, or the modality-specific predictors are themselves poorly calibrated due to limited training data per subset.

falsification_tests.strongest_falsification_test: Propensity-score match patients across clinical contexts (ICU, ward, home) on all observed covariates (age, diagnosis, acuity, medications). Evaluate conditional coverage per context in the matched cohorts using standard marginal conformal prediction. If coverage equalizes across contexts (max-min difference ≤5 points), the proposed mechanism (context as unobserved confounder of X→Y) is falsified; the rival (case-mix differences) is supported.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Conditional coverage does not differ significantly across contexts (p > 0.05, logistic regression of coverage on context after matching) in propensity-score matched cohorts, and standardized mean differences for all covariates <0.1.
falsification_tests.minimum_data_needed: Multi-setting physiological dataset (ICU, ward, home) with ≥200 patients per setting; clinical context labels for all segments; patient covariates for matching (age, diagnosis, acuity score, medications); continuous signals and reference labels; context missingness mechanism (random vs systematic).
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_positive_risk: Equipment differences (invasive vs non-invasive BP) change the measurement target itself across contexts, not just the X→Y relationship; matching on device_type may not fully resolve if the target construct differs.
falsification_tests.most_likely_false_negative_risk: Insufficient overlap in propensity scores across contexts (e.g., ICU patients systematically sicker) prevents adequate matching, or unmeasured confounders (e.g., nursing intensity, undocumented interventions) remain after matching on observed covariates.
